title: People Ops — Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This playbook is Redwood Inference's canonical guide for running predictable, equitable hiring and onboarding processes, and for executing quarterly performance and feedback cycles. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, recruiters, and people-ops partners.

Sections
1) Hiring process and metrics
2) Interview design and rubrics
3) Offer and approval workflow
4) New hire onboarding (0-90 days)
5) Performance cycle and manager responsibilities
6) Policies, templates and escalation paths

1) Hiring process and metrics\nPurpose: Ensure consistent candidate experience, reduce time-to-fill, and improve quality-of-hire.
Target metrics (company-wide):
- Time-to-fill (req opened -> offer accepted): target 45 days
- Time-to-offer (req opened -> offer extended): target 30 days
- Offer acceptance rate: target >= 80%
- Candidate NPS (post-offer survey): target >= 8/10
- Diversity interview slate: at least 30% of screened candidates from underrepresented groups per role (where applicable)

Stages (high level):
1. Requisition & role scoping (Hiring Manager + Recruiter) — job brief, success criteria, compensation band
2. Sourcing & screen (Recruiter) — phone screen, resume pass/fail, diversity sourcing log
3. Interview loop (Interviewers) — technical/role-specific + behavioral + culture fit
4. Debrief & calibration (Hiring Manager + Interviewers + Recruiter) — rubric review
5. Offer & negotiation (Recruiter + Hiring Manager + People Ops)
6. Onboarding & first 90-day plan (Hiring Manager + Onboarding Partner)

Ownership: Recruiter (sourcing, scheduling), Hiring Manager (final decision, hiring plan), People Ops (offer approvals, compensation benchmarking, final paperwork).

2) Interview design and rubrics\nPrinciples: job-focused, consistent, measurable, equitable. Use role-specific rubrics stored in /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples and attach to req.

Interview panel composition guidance:
- IC roles: 1 Hiring Manager, 2-3 peer engineers (one senior), 1 cross-functional partner (product/design/support), 1 recruiter screen
- Manager roles: 2 cross-functional leaders, 1 skip-level, 1 recruiter screen

Rubric example (scale and core dimensions):
| Dimension | Score 1-5 | Focus |
|-----------|-----------|-------|
| Role Competence | 1-5 | Domain knowledge and task execution |
| Problem Solving | 1-5 | Approach, tradeoffs, clarity |
| Communication & Team Fit | 1-5 | Collaboration and feedback |
| Ownership & Impact | 1-5 | Past delivery and scope |

Interviewers must submit scores and written evidence in the ATS within 24 hours. Hiring managers may not make offers until at least 3 interview reports are in the system (exception: small startups/rare skills with approval by Head of Talent).

3) Offer and approval workflow\nSteps:
1. Hiring Manager proposes target level and comp within band.
2. Recruiter prepares offer package (comp, equity guideline, start date, relocation/remote stipends).
3. People Ops approves final comp if > midpoint or requires exception. Approval SLA: 48 business hours.
4. Recruiter extends verbal offer and follows with written offer.
5. Offer negotiation and acceptance recorded in ATS.

Approval matrix:
- Up to midpoint of band: Recruiter + Hiring Manager
- Between midpoint and band top: People Ops approval required
- Above band top: People Ops + CFO sign-off

Negotiation tips for recruiters and managers:
- Use market data (People Ops comp band + market comp spreadsheet)
- Prioritize candidate blocking items (remote flexibility, start date, growth plan) before increasing cash comp

4) New hire onboarding (0-90 days)\nGoals: accelerate time-to-productivity, ensure cultural assimilation, and set clear expectations. Owners: Hiring Manager (role onboarding), Onboarding Partner (logistics), IT (access), Buddy (peer support).

Pre-Start (by Recruiter/People Ops):
- Completed offer paperwork and background check
- Equipment ordered and shipping confirmed (desktop/laptop, monitors, peripherals)
- Account provisioning requests submitted (id, email, Slack, access groups)
- Shared 30/60/90 draft with candidate

Day 0-7 (Orientation):
- Company orientation (People Ops) — mission, org structure, policies, benefits enrollment window
- Manager 1:1 to finalize first-week plan
- Buddy assigned and intro meeting scheduled
- Security & compliance checklist completed (2FA, device encryption)

30-day checklist:
- Role-specific onboarding completed (tech stack access, dev environment, infra runbook links)
- Manager feedback meeting: clear success criteria for 90-day outcomes
- First project assigned (small scope)

60-day checklist:
- Cross-functional introductions completed
- Progress review and adjusted goals
- Identify growth areas and learning plan

90-day checklist:
- 90-day performance review (documented) — manager: recommend continued employment and updated objectives
- Calibration with People Ops if role expectations changed or promotion banding requested

Onboarding templates (links):
- IT access request template: /confluence/eng-infra/cloud-accounts-and-networking/it-access-request
- 30/60/90 template: /confluence/company-handbook/templates/30-60-90-template

5) Performance cycle and manager responsibilities\nCadence:
- Quarterly check-ins (informal) — manager & direct report
- Formal performance reviews: biannual (mid-year + year-end) with calibration windows in May and November
- Career conversations: at least once per quarter for ICs seeking promotion

Manager responsibilities:
- Set clear goals (OKRs or role objectives) with measurable outcomes
- Provide continuous feedback; document coaching conversations in manager notes
- Conduct calibration and submit performance ratings with written justification in People Ops form
- Support career development with concrete growth plans and stretch assignments

Rating scale (example):
- Exceeds Expectations | Meets Expectations | Meets Some Expectations | Below Expectations

Promotion & compensation cycle:
- Promotion nominations follow a written packet: updated role profile, examples of impact, manager recommendation, and peer feedback. Packet due 2 weeks before calibration.
- Compensation adjustments processed during the annual salary review window or as off-cycle with People Ops approval.

6) Policies, templates and escalation paths\nKey policies (summaries):
- Leave & PTO: see /confluence/company-handbook/03_benefits-and-perks for full policy (PTO accrual, parental leave, sabbatical eligibility)
- Work location & hybrid policy: role-based remote eligibility; manager and People Ops must agree for full remote hires in restricted countries
- Background checks & data privacy: all hires require standard background checks where legally permissible; candidate personal data stored in ATS with 7-year retention unless otherwise requested

Escalation matrix (when things go wrong):
- Offer approval delays > 72 business hours: Escalate to Head of Talent (Arjun Patel)
- Equipment not delivered by start date: Escalate to IT lead (eng-infra oncall) and Onboarding Partner
- New hire performance concerns in first 90 days: Manager + People Ops triage meeting within 3 business days; consider Performance Support Plan (PSP)
